judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the footer newsletter field under the heading 'RECEBA NOSSAS INFORMAÇÕES': <input type="email" name="form_fields[email]" placeholder="Digite seu e-mail" required>, with no autocomplete attribute (its accessible name comes from the placeholder because the visually hidden label for="form-field-email" points to the first field with the same duplicated id). claimTrue: the capture shows exactly that, a field for the user's own e-mail and no autocomplete. elementFails: the field collects information about the user (their e-mail to receive the university's news), 'email' is one of the WCAG 2.1 Input Purposes, and HTML supports autocomplete, so 1.3.5 requires the purpose to be programmatically determinable; type="email" only states the data format, not that it is the user's e-mail, and no autocomplete token is present, so the sufficient technique H98 is not met. captureDiffers: the live HTML fetched now has the same input with no autocomplete anywhere on the page, and the screenshot shows the styled footer with this field; the screenshot is taller than the snapshot's bounds (the course grid grew), which does not touch this claim. The claim names the real failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the e-mail field of the 'Dê o primeiro passo na conquista do seu sonho / Fale conosco' contact form (Nome, E-mail, Telefone, ENVIAR): <input type="email" name="form_fields[email]" placeholder="E-mail" required>, no autocomplete. Its captured name 'E-mail E-mail' is what the snapshot computed, because two hidden labels for="form-field-email" (this form's and the footer's, a duplicated id) both point at it; that oddity does not change the claim. claimTrue: the field asks for the user's e-mail and has no autocomplete in the capture. elementFails: the form collects the visitor's own contact data, 'email' is a listed Input Purpose, and nothing identifies the purpose programmatically (type="email" gives the format only; H98's autocomplete="email" is absent), so it fails 1.3.5; the neighbouring Nome and Telefone fields lack autocomplete too. captureDiffers: the live HTML fetched now matches (same input, no autocomplete on the page), and the screenshot shows the styled form as captured. The claim names the real failure.
